title: Generac reports record sales of $1.29 billion, driven by data centers
detail:
Generac reports record sales of $1.29 billion, driven by data centers
Ricardo Torres, Milwaukee Journal Sentinel
Wed, October 28, 2026 at 3:59 PM EDT 2 min read
GNRC
AMZN
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Generac reported record sales as it continues to focus on the hyperscale data center customers.

The Waukesha-based backup power company, reported Oct. 28 sales of $1.29 billion for the quarter, a 16% increase from this point last year. Quarterly profit was $109 million, up from $66 million in 2025.

The results come after Generac announced in September a $8 billion deal with Amazon to supply backup power to Amazon's data centers.

As part of the deal Amazon can buy up to 307,954 shares of Generac at nearly $201 per share.

Generac executives indicated they have another hyperscale data center customer, a company they referred to on a call with investors as "hyperscaler one."

Generac CEO Aaron Jagdfeld said the company has a backlog in data center sales of $4.5 billion, "nearly tripling from 90 days ago."

"More than half (of the backlog) is for 2027, so less than half is for 2028 and that does not include anything for hyperscaler one," Jagdfeld said. "And what (hypercaler one) told us is if we executed, it can be as big or bigger than the $700 million that we anticipate doing with them in 2027."

Jagdfeld said the company has also started negotiations with a third hyperscale data center company which it also did not name, but said there wouldn't be any impact from that company until 2028.

Generac has Amazon orders for 2027 and 2028 which are expected to be worth roughly $2.4 billion.

The stock deal with Amazon brings Generac into better alignment with Amazon "as well as create a material incentive for Amazon to continue leveraging Generac as a supplier well beyond the initial deliveries expected in 2027 and 2028."

"We believe this long-term, strategic collaboration validates our status as the top tier supplier of CNI backup power generators and provides continued confidence in the durability of demand for our products in the data center market," Jagfeld said on the earnings call with analysts and investors.

Jagdfeld said the hyperscale companies "done their own deep due diligence on our supply chain to not only ensure that there's not only redundancy but also capacity in the supply chain so that we can provide products at the level that they're requesting at or higher."

"Hyperscaler one told us they'll go higher in 2028 if we can demonstrate execution in 2027," Jagdfeld said. "We feel good on supply chain, it's obviously tight. Something we watch. But supply chain is an area where we have deep expertise."

title: Amazon’s EPS Is “Absolutely Exploding,” Says Josh Brown. Here’s What the Stock Needs to See October 29

Amazon's EPS Is "Absolutely Exploding," Says Josh Brown. Here's What the Stock Needs to See October 29 ©Dean Drobot via Canva
Key Takeaways

Amazon reports its third-quarter results after the close on Thursday, Oct. 29, with its forward P/E close to its lowest level of the past five years.

Amazon's earnings have grown fast while its stock hasn't kept up, and the low multiple looks like a mispricing as long as AWS keeps growing.

Normalized EPS rose from $2.90 in 2023 to $7.17 in 2025, and analysts expect $13.37 in 2028, while the forward P/E has fallen to 28x against a five-year average of 49x.

The quarter needs to show AWS growing at close to the second quarter's 37% with its margin holding up, which would show the AI spending is paying off.

Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ) reports its third-quarter results after the close on Thursday, Oct. 29, and it goes into the report with an odd setup:

Its earnings keep climbing, and investors keep paying less for them.

Ritholtz Wealth Management CEO Josh Brown summed it up on Tuesday's episode of The Compound and Friends, saying "this company's earnings per share is absolutely exploding. And the stock price has given you nothing as a result of that."

Brown has the earnings right

TIKR's numbers back him up. Amazon's normalized EPS rose from $2.90 in 2023 to $7.17 in 2025, and analysts expect it to keep rising.

Amazon (AMZN): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2023–2028 (TIKR)

Analysts' consensus is $10.43 for 2027 and $13.37 for 2028, close to double what Amazon earned last year. (That's normalized EPS, which leaves out the gains on Amazon's Anthropic stake that have swelled its reported earnings this year.)

The multiple went the other way

Over the same stretch, Amazon's forward P/E has fallen to 28x. That's just above February's five-year low of 26x and far below its five-year average of 49x.

Amazon (AMZN): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

That's nowhere near the kind of valuation that would worry NYU professor Scott Galloway. On Monday's episode of Prof G Markets, he said, "I would want to see these hyperscalers trading at ridiculous valuations, trading at 50, 60, 70 times earnings."

Amazon trades at roughly half the low end of that range.

TIKR tracks 60 analysts on Amazon. How many say "Buy"?

The market is worried about the bill

The discount comes from the cost of the AI build-out. Charles Schwab's Liz Ann Sonders noted on X on Monday that an S&P index of U.S.-listed hyperscalers has fallen by roughly a quarter since early May. Her reason: investors are worried about how all that spending gets paid for.

Amazon AMZN is set to report its third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 29. The company's cloud arm is likely to have remained the central catalyst, even as elevated capital outlays are expected to have weighed on near-term margins. Management's guidance for third-quarter net sales of $197-$202 billion, accompanied by an approximately 80-basis-point foreign-exchange headwind and operating income of $22.5-$26.5 billion, frames a setup in which Amazon Web Services ("AWS") execution carries outsized weight.

Click here to know how the company's overall third-quarter performance is likely to have been.

Amazon.com, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise
Amazon.com, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

Amazon.com, Inc. price-eps-surprise | Amazon.com, Inc. Quote

AWS Acceleration and Backlog Strength

AWS is likely to have sustained the accelerating trajectory established in the second quarter of 2026, when AWS revenues climbed 37% year over year to $42.2 billion, marking the fastest growth in 18 quarters at an annualized run rate of $169 billion. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for third-quarter AWS revenues is pegged at $45.4 billion, indicating 37.5% year-over-year growth.

The disclosed AWS backlog of $496 billion, growing at a triple-digit percentage rate year over year as of the end of the second quarter, provided multi-year demand visibility. Management's commentary that capacity would still fall short of 2026 demand strengthens the case for sustained momentum. AWS' AI and custom chips businesses, each surpassing a $25 billion run rate, signal competitive resilience against scaled cloud rivals Microsoft MSFT Azure, Alphabet GOOGL-owned Google Cloud and Oracle ORCL. According to data from Synergy Research Group, Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet held second-quarter 2026 worldwide cloud market shares of 28%, 20% and 15%, respectively. Microsoft and Alphabet are steadily narrowing the gap, applying sustained competitive pressure on AWS.

Strategic Partnerships of AWS in Q3

The third quarter brought several high-profile agreements that are likely to have shaped AWS' near-term positioning. Most notably, AWS and NVIDIA expanded their partnership in August to deploy two million additional NVIDIA GPUs during 2027-2028. AWS also signed a multi-year strategic collaboration agreement with Cognition, expanded its partnership with Salesforce, and agreed to acquire DuckLabs. Additionally, AWS became the first cloud provider approved for NATO RESTRICTED workloads across all member nations, while Agentic Grid Planning, built with Duke Energy, broadened the customer base across defense and utilities.
